stem: A healthy adult female of average height (5 ft 6 in) is most likely to have a pelvic inlet of which Caldwell-Moloy type?
explanation: The gynaecoid pelvis (about 50% of women) has a round inlet and is the typical female pelvis, the most favourable for vaginal delivery.

stem: A woman in labour at term has an oval-shaped pelvic inlet on clinical pelvimetry, with the anteroposterior diameter smaller than the transverse diameter. The baby is occipitoposterior. What type of pelvis does she most likely have?
explanation: A platypelloid pelvis has a flattened inlet with a short anteroposterior and wide transverse diameter. The anthropoid pelvis is the opposite (AP longer than transverse) and favours occipitoposterior positions.
key_note: The stem is internally inconsistent (OP position suggests anthropoid); the paper key D follows the stated AP smaller than transverse, i.e. platypelloid.

stem: Which of the following is the normal transverse diameter of the pelvic inlet?
explanation: The transverse diameter is the widest diameter of the inlet (about 13 to 13.5 cm), whereas the obstetric conjugate is about 11 cm.
key_note: Textbooks quote 12.5 to 13.5 cm; the paper key 13.5 cm is kept.

stem: A primigravida has an adequate pelvic outlet, but there may be a problem in the midpelvis as the head is not engaged at 39 weeks. What is the normal interspinous diameter of a gynaecoid pelvis?

options.E: Interspinous diameter is not a useful clinical assessment

explanation: The interspinous diameter (about 10 to 10.5 cm) is the narrowest part of the pelvic cavity; less than 8 cm suggests midpelvic contraction.
key_note: Not marked in the source paper; answer by reviewer.

stem: Which of the following is likely to be associated with a contracted pelvis?
explanation: Rickets (vitamin D deficiency) causes pelvic deformity, typically a flat platypelloid pelvis. A pendulous abdomen in a primigravida is a sign that may point to contracted pelvis, not a cause of it.
key_note: Some paper keys marked C (pendulous abdomen); correct is E: rickets is the classic cause of a contracted pelvis.

stem: Which best describes the reproductive history of a woman at 12 weeks of gestation with a previous twin delivery and a stillbirth at 27 weeks?
explanation: Gravidity counts pregnancies (twin pregnancy, stillbirth, current = 3). Parity counts deliveries beyond viability, so strictly she is G3P2; of the options offered, G3P3 is the only one with the correct gravidity.
key_note: Strictly G3P2 (a twin birth counts as one parity), which is not offered; paper key G3P3 is kept as the best available option.

stem: Which statement is correct regarding calculating the expected date of delivery (EDD)?

options.B: The last menstrual period (LMP) is reliable if the cycles are irregular
options.C: The average length of pregnancy is 280 days
options.D: LMP-defined dates are more accurate than those calculated from ultrasound
options.E: Head circumference may be used to date a pregnancy until 25 weeks

explanation: Pregnancy is dated from the LMP and lasts on average 280 days (40 weeks). Early ultrasound (crown-rump length) is more accurate than LMP, and LMP is unreliable with irregular cycles.

stem: An 18-year-old G2P1 with the first day of her last menstrual period on May 7 presents for her first antenatal visit at 10 weeks. What is her estimated date of delivery?
explanation: Naegele's rule: add 7 days to the first day of the LMP and subtract 3 months (add 9 months), giving May 7 to February 14 of the next year.

stem: A woman has a positive pregnancy test and her LMP was June 30. Her expected date of delivery is approximately:
explanation: Naegele's rule: June 30 plus 7 days minus 3 months gives about April 6 to 7.
key_note: One paper key marked C (March 7); correct is A (Naegele's rule). Same question as the O1 item for LMP June 30.

stem: A 28-year-old at 20 weeks of gestation has a fundal height at the umbilicus. What does this indicate?
explanation: The fundus reaches the umbilicus at about 20 to 22 weeks, and fundal height in cm approximates the gestational age in weeks after 20 weeks, so this is normal.

stem: In a cephalic presentation, the position is determined by the relationship of which fetal part to the maternal pelvis?
explanation: The denominator of a vertex presentation is the occiput (mentum in face, sacrum in breech, acromion in shoulder).
key_note: Not marked in the source paper; answer by reviewer.

stem: A labouring patient has a cervix 5 cm dilated, intact membranes and an engaged head. Engagement is best defined as:

options.A: When the presenting part goes through the pelvic inlet
options.B: When the presenting part is at the level of the ischial spines
options.C: When the greatest biparietal diameter of the fetal head passes through the pelvic inlet
options.D: When the greatest biparietal diameter of the head is at the level of the ischial spines
options.E: When the greatest diameter of the presenting part passes through the narrowest part of the pelvis

explanation: The head is engaged when its widest transverse diameter (biparietal) has passed through the pelvic inlet, usually felt as less than 2/5 palpable per abdomen.
key_note: Not marked in the source paper; answer by reviewer.

stem: A 24-year-old pregnant woman attends for an antenatal check-up; her LMP was 3 March 2020. What is her EDD?
explanation: Naegele's rule: add 7 days to the LMP and add 9 months (subtract 3 months): 3 March becomes 10 December 2020.
